bolt-spain.label: Spain — Balearics & Costa Brava
bolt-spain.summary: Spain is Europe's #1 leisure-boating and second-busiest tourism market, with the densest island-and-coast water demand in the western Med — the Balearics, the Costa Brava and the Costa del Sol — almost none of it monetised in-app. Bolt already runs ride-hail across Spanish cities; the water tier is the missing leg between the airport pier and the island.

hero.title: Bolt × Navier — Spain, the western-Med island shuttle
hero.subtitle: Turn the Balearic and Costa crossings into a flying, in-app water tier.
hero.what_we_do_together: A Bolt-branded foiling water tier across the Balearics, the Costa Brava and the Costa del Sol — booked in the same app as the car, all-electric, no wake, no diesel-ferry timetable.

bolt-spain.why_now: Spain hosts ~85M visitors a year and the Balearics alone draw ~16M; the islands are choking on diesel ferries and rental cars while Formentera, Mallorca and Ibiza tighten anchoring and emissions rules. A clean, quiet, on-demand foiling hop is exactly what the regulators and the resorts are asking for — and no super-app has the water leg.
bolt-spain.multimodal_fit: Same Bolt app, same wallet: a Bolt car to the pier, a foiling Pioneer II across the water, a Bolt scooter on the island. The water leg books door-to-door, captain-partners instead of driver-partners.
bolt-spain.partner_context: Bolt is the largest European-owned mobility platform, already operating ride-hail and micromobility across Spain. Spain is a top-five Bolt market by trips and the natural place to prove a Med water tier before extending east.
bolt-spain.why_navier_now: Pioneer II is commercial now and clears the short Balearic and Costa hops on a single charge; the Palma–Ibiza–Menorca regional legs (75–130nm) come into reach with Quanta-LR on the 2026+ roadmap. Spain's berths already exist — Palma, Ibiza Town, Formentera (La Savina), Puerto Banús — so we need a pedestal, not a port.
bolt-spain.differentiation: Against the diesel fast-ferry: half the door-to-door time, zero wake into protected Posidonia seagrass zones, no fixed timetable, and a fare booked in an app riders already have. Against a private RIB charter: a fraction of the cost and fully electric.

proof_points.claim: The Balearics are a top global leisure-marine market.
proof_points.evidence: Mallorca, Ibiza, Menorca and Formentera draw ~16M visitors a year with intense inter-island and coast-to-island water demand.

proof_points.claim: The corridors are protected and emissions-sensitive.
proof_points.evidence: Formentera caps daily vehicles and the Balearic Posidonia decree restricts anchoring and wake — favouring a quiet, electric, foiling hull.

proof_points.claim: The berths already exist.
proof_points.evidence: Palma, Ibiza Town, La Savina (Formentera), Port de Sóller, Puerto Banús and Marbella are working harbours — Pioneer II needs only a berth pedestal.

proof_points.claim: Bolt already owns the rider in Spain.
proof_points.evidence: Bolt operates ride-hail and micromobility across Spanish cities; the water leg slots into an app riders already carry.

objections.concern: The Balearic crossings (Palma–Ibiza) are too long for an 8-pax foiler.
objections.response: Correct — those 75–130nm legs are explicitly Quanta-LR (roadmap), never faked on a Pioneer II. The near-term business is the dense ≤70nm island-and-coast capillary network where Pioneer II is commercial today.
On fixed timetables, with diesel wake into protected zones, and no door-to-door app booking. The foiling hop wins on time, experience and emissions, and is bookable on demand in the Bolt app.

objections.concern: Seasonality — Spain's water demand is summer-heavy.
objections.response: True, and the model sizes the Prove fleet to the shoulder-season floor; summer is upside. The same hulls redeploy across the Med as the network grows.

bolt-spain.the_ask: Co-brand a Spain water tier with Bolt, starting with a 2-boat Prove fleet on the Costa del Sol / Costa Brava capillary hops in 2026 H2, scaling across the Balearic islands as berth agreements land.
bolt-spain.close: Spain is the densest leisure-water market in Europe and Bolt already owns the rider. The water tier is the one leg no one has flown — let's fly it.
bolt-spain.end_state: A western-Med foiling network — Costa Brava, Costa del Sol and the Balearics — booked in the Bolt app, with Quanta-LR closing the inter-island regional legs.

bolt-egypt.label: Egypt — Cairo & Red Sea
bolt-egypt.summary: Egypt pairs two distinct, dense water markets: the Red Sea resort coast (Hurghada, El Gouna, Sahl Hasheesh, Sharm El Sheikh) where reef-and-resort hops are the core leisure economy, and the Nile through Greater Cairo, a 20-million-person city split by a river it barely uses for transport. Bolt is a leading ride-hail brand in Egypt; the water tier monetises both.

hero.title: Bolt × Navier — Egypt, Red Sea reefs and the Cairo Nile
hero.subtitle: Fly the reef hops and the river commute, in the Bolt app.
hero.what_we_do_together: A Bolt-branded foiling water tier on the Red Sea resort coast and the Cairo Nile — all-electric reef-and-resort hops and a flying river link across Greater Cairo.

bolt-egypt.why_now: Egypt is targeting 30M tourists, with the Red Sea its fastest-growing coast and a new wave of resort and marina development at El Gouna, Sahl Hasheesh and the Red Sea Riviera. Meanwhile Greater Cairo's road congestion is among the worst on earth and the Nile is wide, calm and almost unused for transport. Both are textbook foiling corridors.
bolt-egypt.multimodal_fit: Same Bolt app, same wallet: a Bolt car to the marina or corniche pier, a foiling Pioneer II across the reef or the river, a Bolt car on arrival.
bolt-egypt.partner_context: Bolt operates ride-hail at scale across Egyptian cities including Cairo. Egypt is a high-trip, price-sensitive market where the water leg adds a premium tier without new app behaviour.
bolt-egypt.why_navier_now: Every core Red Sea and Cairo corridor is ≤16nm — squarely Pioneer II, commercial today. The piers exist: El Gouna's lagoon network, Hurghada Marina, Sharm's jetties, and the Cairo corniche. No regional Quanta-LR leg is needed to start.
bolt-egypt.differentiation: Against the diesel excursion boat: faster to the reefs, no fumes over protected coral, and bookable on demand. Against the Cairo road: a flying river crossing that sidesteps the bridges entirely.

bolt-egypt.close: Two dense, ready water markets in one country — reef hops and a river city of 20 million. Bolt has the rider; Navier has the boat.
bolt-egypt.end_state: A Red Sea foiling network plus a flying Cairo river link, both booked in the Bolt app.

bolt-sweden.label: Sweden — Stockholm archipelago
bolt-sweden.summary: Stockholm is built on 14 islands across an archipelago of ~30,000 — a city that should move on water but mostly doesn't, beyond a handful of diesel commuter ferries. Bolt's home region is the Baltic, and Stockholm is a flagship Bolt market; a clean, foiling, in-app water tier is a natural fit for both the city commute and the archipelago leisure runs.

hero.title: Bolt × Navier — Stockholm, the archipelago water tier
hero.subtitle: Fly the commute across the islands, in the Bolt app.
hero.what_we_do_together: A Bolt-branded foiling water tier across central Stockholm and the inner archipelago — all-electric, no wake, booked in the same app as the car.

bolt-sweden.why_now: Stockholm has ambitious climate-neutral targets, a congested island core, and a strong existing water-commute culture that runs on ageing diesel tonnage. The city is actively electrifying its ferries — an open door for a quiet, fast, zero-emission foiling tier on the dense inner-water legs.
bolt-sweden.multimodal_fit: Same Bolt app, same wallet: a Bolt ride to the quay, a foiling Pioneer II across the water, a Bolt scooter on the far island. The water leg books door-to-door.
bolt-sweden.partner_context: Bolt is an Estonian company and the dominant European-owned mobility platform across the Nordics and Baltics; Stockholm is a flagship market. A water tier extends Bolt's home-region leadership onto the water it knows best.
bolt-sweden.why_navier_now: Every core central-Stockholm and inner-archipelago leg is ≤12nm — Pioneer II, commercial now. The quays already exist (Slussen, Nybroplan, Strömkajen, Stadshuskajen). The Åland crossing (75nm) is a Quanta-LR roadmap leg, never faked on a Pioneer II.
bolt-sweden.differentiation: Against the diesel commuter ferry: faster, quieter, zero-emission, and bookable on demand instead of by timetable. Against the road-and-bridge commute: a direct flying line across water the city is already organised around.

proof_points.claim: Stockholm is a natural water-transport city.
proof_points.evidence: The city spans 14 islands with an established commuter-ferry culture and a 30,000-island archipelago beyond.

proof_points.claim: The city is electrifying its waterborne transport.
proof_points.evidence: Stockholm has active programmes to decarbonise its ferries and meet climate-neutral targets — directly favouring an electric foiler.

proof_points.claim: The quays already exist.
proof_points.evidence: Slussen, Nybroplan, Strömkajen, Stadshuskajen and Djurgården are working passenger quays — Pioneer II needs only a berth pedestal.

proof_points.claim: Stockholm is a flagship Bolt market in Bolt's home region.
proof_points.evidence: Bolt operates ride-hail and micromobility across the Nordics/Baltics from its Estonian base.

objections.response: On diesel, on fixed timetables, with no app booking. The foiling tier wins on speed, emissions and on-demand convenience, and complements rather than replaces the trunk ferry routes.
Central hops compete on time saved against a congested island core, and the archipelago leisure runs (Vaxholm, Drottningholm) carry a clear leisure premium.

bolt-sweden.the_ask: Co-brand a Stockholm water tier with Bolt, launching a 2-boat Prove fleet on the central inner-city hops in 2026 H2, scaling into the inner archipelago as quay agreements land.
bolt-sweden.close: Stockholm is a water city that forgot to fly. Bolt owns the home-region rider; Navier brings the boat. Let's put the archipelago in the app.
bolt-sweden.end_state: A foiling inner-Stockholm and inner-archipelago network in the Bolt app, with Quanta-LR opening the Åland crossing.

bolt-cyprus.label: Cyprus — Limassol, Larnaca & Paphos
bolt-cyprus.summary: Cyprus pairs a year-round Mediterranean climate with three resort poles — Ayia Napa/Protaras, Larnaca and Limassol/Paphos — strung along a coast where the road network forces long inland detours between beaches that sit minutes apart by water. Bolt is already a leading ridehail brand on the island; a foiling water tier turns the airport-to-resort and resort-to-resort transfers into the fastest, cleanest leg of the trip.

hero.title: Bolt × Navier — Cyprus, the sun-coast water shuttle
hero.subtitle: Foil the Ayia Napa, Larnaca and Limassol coast at airport speed, booked in the Bolt app.
hero.what_we_do_together: A Bolt-branded electric-foiling tier across Cyprus's three resort clusters — airport-to-resort hops, beach-to-beach shuttles, and a Quanta-LR regional spine linking Limassol and Larnaca, with a roadmap leg across to Lebanon.

bolt-cyprus.why_now: Cyprus draws ~4M visitors a year against a population of ~0.9M, heavily concentrated in summer along a thin coastal strip. The Ayia Napa–Protaras and Larnaca–Ayia Napa roads choke every July; the water beside them is empty and flat. Pioneer II is commercial now and clears the dense southern-coast hops today.
bolt-cyprus.multimodal_fit: Same Bolt app and wallet: a Bolt car from the terminal to the marina, a foiling hop to the resort, a Bolt scooter for the last 300m. Cyprus is small enough that a single multimodal chain can own the entire arrival journey.
bolt-cyprus.partner_context: Bolt operates ridehail across Cyprus and has deep brand trust with both residents and the large tourist inflow. Marine adds a premium, weather-resilient tier on exactly the corridors where summer road congestion is worst — without Bolt touching a hull.
bolt-cyprus.why_navier_now: Pioneer II (8 pax, commercial now) covers the ≤70nm southern-coast and airport-resort legs immediately. The Limassol–Larnaca regional run (35nm) is comfortably in Pioneer range; the Larnaca–Beirut crossing (115nm) is explicitly a Quanta-LR roadmap leg, never faked on a 70nm boat.
bolt-cyprus.differentiation: Against the airport taxi: comparable door-to-door cost at a fraction of the time in peak season, zero local emissions, and a view. Against the diesel excursion boat: quiet, foiling, on-demand and in-app rather than fixed-departure.

proof_points.evidence: ~4M annual visitors against ~0.9M residents, concentrated on the southern resort coast in summer.

proof_points.claim: The resort poles are minutes apart by water but long by road.
proof_points.evidence: Larnaca–Ayia Napa is ~19nm of flat water versus a congested summer road; Limassol–Larnaca ~35nm.

proof_points.claim: Bolt already has ridehail demand and brand on the island.
proof_points.evidence: Established Bolt ridehail footprint across Cypriot cities provides the demand graph to upsell water.

proof_points.claim: Year-round operability.
proof_points.evidence: Mild Mediterranean winters extend the foiling season well beyond the July–August peak.

objections.concern: The Larnaca–Beirut leg is too long for an 8-pax foiler.
objections.response: Correct — that 115nm crossing is explicitly a Quanta-LR (700nm-class) roadmap corridor, rendered aspirational. Phase 1 and 2 run only on Pioneer-range water; nothing long is faked on a 70nm boat.
Peak is summer, but Cyprus's mild winters keep the southern-coast corridors operable year-round, and airport-resort transfer demand persists through shoulder seasons.
We anchor one cluster (Ayia Napa) first to prove unit economics, then replicate the proven playbook to Larnaca and Limassol rather than spreading thin from day one.

bolt-cyprus.the_ask: Co-brand a Cyprus water tier with Bolt, launching a 2-boat Pioneer II anchor in the Ayia Napa/Protaras cluster, with a committed scale path to Larnaca and Limassol and a Quanta-LR regional spine.
bolt-cyprus.close: Cyprus is a compact, year-round, tourism-dense island where the road is the bottleneck and the water is the shortcut — an ideal proving ground for a Bolt-branded foiling tier.
bolt-cyprus.end_state: A three-cluster Cypriot water network — Ayia Napa, Larnaca and Limassol — with a Quanta-LR regional spine and an aspirational Levant crossing, all booked in the Bolt app.

bolt-south-africa.label: South Africa — Cape Town (Table Bay & False Bay)
bolt-south-africa.summary: Cape Town is Africa's premier coastal city, wrapped around Table Bay with the V&A Waterfront — one of the continent's most-visited destinations — as its anchor. The high-volume Robben Island heritage ferry, the Hout Bay and Simon's Town marine-wildlife harbours and the dramatic peninsula coastline make a natural premium leisure-and-heritage water market. Bolt is well established across South Africa; a co-branded foiling tier turns the waterfront and peninsula crossings into a fast, clean, in-app signature experience.

hero.what_we_do_together: A Bolt-branded electric-foiling tier across Table Bay and False Bay — heritage crossings to Robben Island and premium peninsula leisure runs — anchored at the V&A Waterfront.

bolt-south-africa.why_now: Cape Town is a high-profile global tourism brand with huge waterfront footfall and a constant high-volume heritage ferry to Robben Island. Bolt is established across South Africa, so the app and riders are already here. Pioneer II clears the sheltered Table Bay and False Bay corridors; routing flexes around the Cape's wind exactly as the existing tour operators already do.
bolt-south-africa.multimodal_fit: Same Bolt app: a Bolt car to the V&A Waterfront, a foiling crossing to Robben Island or a peninsula run to Hout Bay, a Bolt ride on arrival — the iconic Cape Town water experience, in-app.
bolt-south-africa.partner_context: Bolt is well established across South Africa (Cape Town, Johannesburg, Durban). Cape Town's premium tourism footfall and high willingness-to-pay make a co-branded heritage-and-leisure water tier a strong, brand-led African flagship.
bolt-south-africa.why_navier_now: The sheltered corridors are in Pioneer II range today: V&A–Robben Island (~7nm), V&A–Hout Bay (~12nm), Hout Bay–Simon's Town (~22nm) and Cape Town–Gordon's Bay (~30nm). Quanta-LR is held in reserve for the longer exposed-coast corridors — never faked on the all-electric boat.
bolt-south-africa.differentiation: Against the diesel tour boat: a faster, smoother, zero-emission crossing aligned with the Cape's marine-protected-area focus — and against the road, a premium peninsula link that skips the coastal drive, all in the Bolt app.
